subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
summary: Blood relations (pointing/photograph statements, coded relations, family puzzles) and direction sense (turns, rotations through angles, shortest distance, shadows and direction-mapping). Both are solved reliably by drawing: a family tree with fixed symbols, or a path on a compass grid with Pythagoras for the final distance.

sections.heading: Relationship vocabulary
sections.body:
Most mistakes in blood-relation questions come from vague vocabulary. Fix these meanings:
- **Paternal** = on the father's side; **maternal** = on the mother's side.
- Father's or mother's brother = **uncle**; father's or mother's sister = **aunt**. Uncle's or aunt's child = **cousin**.
- Brother's or sister's son = **nephew**; daughter = **niece**.
- Wife's or husband's brother, or sister's husband = **brother-in-law**; wife's or husband's sister, or brother's wife = **sister-in-law**.
- Son's wife = **daughter-in-law**; daughter's husband = **son-in-law**.
- Father's father = **grandfather**; son's son or daughter's son = **grandson**.
- 'Only son of my father' (said by a man) = the speaker himself; 'only daughter of my mother' (said by a woman) = the speaker herself.

Gender matters: a relation like 'sibling', 'child' or 'spouse' does not tell you whether the person is male or female. If the gender of a person is never given, the answer may be 'cannot be determined'.

sections.heading: Drawing a family tree
sections.body:
Use the same symbols every time so that you can read the tree at a glance: + for male, − for female, = for a married couple, a vertical line for parent-child (one generation down) and a horizontal line for siblings. Keep each generation on its own row.

**Method for pointing / photograph questions**: start from the end of the sentence and move backwards. In 'She is the daughter of my son's wife': my son's wife is my daughter-in-law; her daughter is my granddaughter (assuming she is also my son's child, as exam questions do).

**Coded relations** (A + B means A is the father of B, etc.): translate each symbol into a short sentence, draw the tree in order from left to right, then read off the asked relation.

**Family puzzles** ('a family has 3 fathers, 2 mothers ...'): one person can play several roles - a man can be a father, a son and a brother at the same time. Build the smallest tree that satisfies all counts, starting from the oldest generation.

diagram.title: Family-tree notation
diagram.ascii:
Notation:  (+) male   (-) female   =  married couple
           |  one generation down   --  siblings

              D(+)
               |
              C(?)
               |
          A(+) -- B(-)

A is the son of C, so A is the grandson of D.

sections.heading: Coded relations and puzzles: worked approach
sections.body:
For a chain like P $ Q # R @ S, read it two letters at a time: P $ Q, then Q # R, then R @ S. Each link adds one person to the tree. After drawing all links, find the two people asked about and count generations between them:
- Same generation: brother, sister, cousin, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, husband, wife.
- One generation up: father, mother, uncle, aunt, father-in-law.
- Two generations up: grandfather, grandmother.
- One generation down: son, daughter, nephew, niece.

Then decide the side (direct line or through a sibling or marriage) and the gender. Exams usually assume that the wife of a father is the mother of his children; follow this convention unless the question says 'step'.

In 'which of the following means A is the niece of B' questions, test each option by drawing; stop as soon as one option gives a female in the generation below B, through B's sibling.

sections.heading: Directions, turns and rotations
sections.body:
There are four main directions (N, E, S, W) and four corners (NE, SE, SW, NW). Treat directions as angles measured clockwise from North: N = 0°, NE = 45°, E = 90°, SE = 135°, S = 180°, SW = 225°, W = 270°, NW = 315°.
- A **right turn** adds 90° (clockwise); a **left turn** subtracts 90° (anticlockwise).
- For rotations, compute the **net angle**: clockwise angles positive, anticlockwise negative; reduce modulo 360°. A rotation of 362° clockwise equals 2° clockwise.
- Facing North, your right is East; facing South, your right is West; facing East, your right is South; facing West, your right is North.

**Direction mapping** questions ('if North becomes East and South becomes West, what does North-west become?') are one fixed rotation: N → E is 90° clockwise, so every direction moves 90° clockwise and NW (315°) becomes 315 + 90 = 405 − 360 = 45° = **NE**. If the given pairs are not a rotation (e.g. a reflection where East and West swap), map each direction by the same reflection.

diagram.title: Compass with angles
diagram.ascii:
N (0°)
        NW     |     NE
          \    |    /
  W (270°) ----+---- E (90°)
          /    |    \
        SW     |     SE
               S (180°)

Right turn = 90° clockwise; left turn = 90° anticlockwise

sections.heading: Distance and final position
sections.body:
Draw each leg of the walk on a rough grid. Keep a running **x** (east positive) and **y** (north positive):
- North adds to y, South subtracts from y, East adds to x, West subtracts from x.

At the end:
- **Shortest distance** from the start = √(x² + y²) (Pythagoras). Common triples: 3-4-5, 6-8-10, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25.
- **Direction from the start**: the signs of x and y give the quadrant (x > 0, y > 0 → North-east; x < 0, y > 0 → North-west, and so on). If x = 0 or y = 0, the answer is a main direction.
- 'Direction of the start from the end point' is the **opposite** of 'direction of the end point from the start'.

In 'A is to the west of B, C is to the south of B ...' questions, place one person at the origin and plot the others in order; distances may not be given, so judge only the direction.

**Shadows**: the Sun rises in the east, so in the **morning shadows fall towards the west**; in the **evening they fall towards the east**. If a person's shadow falls to his left in the morning, the left is west, so he is facing north.

sections.heading: Relative-position questions with several people
sections.body:
Questions such as 'P is 5 m east of Q, R is 3 m north of P ...' are solved by fixing one person at the origin (0, 0) and placing every other person with coordinates, exactly as in a walk.

Example: P is 5 m east of Q. R is 3 m north of P. S is 5 m west of R. Where is S with respect to Q?
- Q = (0, 0); P = (5, 0); R = (5, 3); S = (5 − 5, 3) = (0, 3).
- S has the same x as Q and is 3 m higher, so **S is 3 m north of Q**.

When no distances are given ('A is west of K, B is south of K, L is between A and K'), mark relative positions only. If the answer depends on an unknown distance (for example, whether a point is north-east or exactly east), the correct option may be 'cannot be determined'.

For questions with a person **facing** a direction and others standing to his left or right, convert left/right into compass directions first (facing South: left = East, right = West), then plot.

formulas.name: Shortest distance
formulas.note: x = net east-west displacement, y = net north-south displacement.

formulas.name: Net rotation
formulas.formula: Net angle = Σ clockwise − Σ anticlockwise (mod 360°)
formulas.note: Positive result = clockwise from the original direction.

formulas.name: Shadow rule
formulas.formula: Morning: shadow → West; Evening: shadow → East
formulas.note: Sun rises in the east, sets in the west.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: Pointing to a man, Riya (a woman) says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the man related to Riya?
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: 'The only daughter of my mother', said by a woman, is Riya herself.
Step 2: So the man's mother is Riya.
Answer: the man is Riya's **son**.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: A # B means A is the father of B; A @ B means A is the sister of B; A $ B means A is the wife of B. In P $ Q # R @ S, how is P related to S?
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: P $ Q - P is the wife of Q.
Step 2: Q # R - Q is the father of R.
Step 3: R @ S - R is the sister of S, so S is also a child of Q.
Step 4: P is Q's wife, so P is the mother of Q's children.
Answer: P is S's **mother**.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: A is the brother of B. B is the daughter of C. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: B is C's daughter and A is B's brother, so A is C's son.
Step 2: D is C's father, so D is two generations above A.
Step 3: A is male.
Answer: A is D's **grandson**.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: Ravi walks 10 km north, turns right and walks 8 km, then turns right again and walks 4 km. How far and in which direction is he from the start?
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: North 10 → (x, y) = (0, 10).
Step 2: Right from North is East: 8 km → (8, 10).
Step 3: Right from East is South: 4 km → (8, 6).
Step 4: Distance = √(8² + 6²) = √(64 + 36) = √100 = **10 km**.
Step 5: x > 0 and y > 0, so he is **North-east** of the start.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: Meena faces West. She turns 135° clockwise and then 270° anticlockwise. Which direction does she face now?
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: Net rotation = +135° − 270° = −135°, i.e. 135° anticlockwise.
Step 2: West = 270°. 270° − 135° = 135°.
Step 3: 135° = **South-east**.
Check by stepping anticlockwise from West: 45° → SW, 90° → S, 135° → SE.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: In the morning, Amit and Sunil stand facing each other. Amit's shadow falls exactly to Sunil's right. Which direction is Sunil facing?
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: In the morning the Sun is in the east, so shadows fall towards the west.
Step 2: Amit's shadow points west, and it lies to Sunil's right, so Sunil's right hand points west.
Step 3: A person whose right is west is facing **South**. (Amit, facing Sunil, faces North.)

pitfalls: Assuming gender from a relation word like 'child' or 'sibling'; check whether gender is actually given.
Reading a chain in a pointing statement from the front; work from the end of the sentence backwards.
Missing that 'only daughter of my mother' said by a woman refers to herself.
Confusing 'direction of A from B' with 'direction of B from A'; they are opposite.
Adding anticlockwise rotations as clockwise; take clockwise as + and anticlockwise as −.
Taking the left/right of a person facing South as the same as the reader's left/right.
Reversing the shadow rule: morning shadows fall to the west, not east.
quickRevision: Symbols for trees: + male, − female, = couple, | generation, -- siblings.
Pointing statements: decode from the end backwards.
Uncle/aunt one generation up; nephew/niece one generation down.
Spouse of a parent is assumed to be the other parent unless 'step' is said.
Directions as angles: N 0°, E 90°, S 180°, W 270°.
Right turn +90°, left turn −90°; net rotation mod 360°.
Facing North: right = East; facing South: right = West.
Morning shadow falls west; evening shadow falls east.
Direction mapping: find the rotation from one given pair and apply it to all.
Direction of start from end = opposite of direction of end from start.
